speaker_role: independent college admissions strategist/consultant ('Sara Harberson - America's College Counselor'), with a University of Pennsylvania admissions background referenced
commercial_incentive: Promotes her paid 'Application Nation' program, book, and blog throughout; live Q&A content is free but repeatedly funnels toward paid offerings
key_insights: Common App activity descriptions are limited to 150 characters, not words, so distinct achievements (e.g. a Girl Scout Gold Award project) should get their own activity listing rather than being folded into a related one
Athletic awards should go in the activities section tied to that sport, not the academic honors section, to avoid repeating ('hammering') the same accomplishment twice

Supplemental essays are said to matter roughly as much as the Common App main essay at highly selective schools with required supplements, but less at higher-acceptance-rate schools with optional ones
Common App removed the question about where older siblings attended college; some individual college supplements still ask about family attendance

Students considering a gap year should still apply as high school seniors, secure a deposit, then formally request a deferral (typically due around June 1st) rather than delaying application by a year
Rolling-admissions schools (e.g. Alabama, UCF, Pittsburgh, Arizona) reward applying as early as possible; fixed-deadline schools (ED/EA/RD) generally don't reward submitting well before the deadline
The cumulative GPA colleges typically evaluate covers 9th-11th grade (not senior year); some schools (e.g. Carnegie Mellon, UC system) exclude 9th grade from GPA calculation entirely

The Common Data Set's Section C ('level of applicant's interest') can indicate whether a school tracks demonstrated interest, though some schools mark it as considered while saying they don't track visits, tying it more to early-decision behavior instead
specific_numbers_or_facts: Common App activity description limit: 150 characters, not words (per Sara Harberson)
Gap year deferral request deadline typically 'around June 1st' (per Sara Harberson)
Common App COVID-impact explanation section allows 'up to 250 words' (per Sara Harberson)
Illustrative SAT benchmark discussed for Boston College nursing/arts & sciences: ~1500 ideal, 1480 described as 'super close' (per Sara Harberson, her own estimate)
notable_or_distinctive: Extremely granular, mechanics-level Common App advice (character limits, section placement rules, GPA calculation windows) delivered via rapid-fire live audience Q&A.
reliability_notes: Single consultant's opinions and interpretations, some explicitly her personal recommendation rather than official policy; specific numeric benchmarks for particular colleges are her own estimates, not published data; policy specifics may shift year to year.
